styleWhy: Coffee's story is geography: a belt of growing countries around the equator and the sea routes that carry the beans north, which a map shows at a glance.

copy.idea: Where the world's coffee comes from: the band of tropical countries that grow it, the few that dominate, and the routes that carry it to the cups of Europe and North America.
copy.hook: About 184 million bags of coffee are grown in a year. Where?
copy.body:
About 184 million 60-kilo bags of coffee were produced in 2025/26.

It grows in more than 40 countries, mostly in a band around the equator, between the tropics: the coffee belt.

One country leads by far: Brazil grows nearly 40% of the world's coffee.

Next come Vietnam, mostly robusta, then Colombia, Ethiopia and Indonesia.

Coffee's story begins in Ethiopia, where ancient coffee forests still grow.

From the belt, the beans sail north: the European Union and the United States are the biggest importers.

Every cup, a long journey.

facts.text: World coffee production is estimated at about 184 million 60-kg bags in coffee year 2025/26 (183.6 million, up from 175.9 million in 2024/25, ICO Table 3). Quote: "World coffee production is estimated to increase by 4.4% to 183.6 million bags in the current coffee year 2025/26".
facts.source: International Coffee Organization, Coffee Market Report, August 2026, https://www.ico.org/documents/cy2025-26/cmr-0826-e.pdf

facts.text: Coffee is grown in more than 40 countries, mostly between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn (the 'coffee belt'). Quote: "In more than 40 countries, mostly in a narrow climactic zone along the Equator between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn (25°N to 30°S)!"
facts.source: National Coffee Association USA, 'Coffee Regions of the World', aboutcoffee.org, modified 31 July 2026, https://aboutcoffee.org/origins/coffee-regions-of-the-world/

facts.text: Brazil is the largest producer, with nearly 40% of world output. Quote: "Brazil accounts for nearly 40 percent of world production".
facts.source: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Coffee: World Markets and Trade, July 2026, https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/circulars/coffee.pdf

facts.text: The top five producers (2026/27 forecast) are, in order, Brazil, Vietnam, Colombia, Ethiopia ("a record 12.1 million" bags) and Indonesia (11.4 million); Vietnam grows mostly robusta (Robusta 31,400 of 32,500 thousand bags).
facts.source: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Coffee: World Markets and Trade, July 2026, https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/circulars/coffee.pdf

facts.text: Coffee was first discovered in Ethiopia. Quote: "the benefits of coffee beans and brewed coffee were first discovered on the Ethiopian Plateau, where ancient coffee forests still thrive today."
facts.source: National Coffee Association USA, aboutcoffee.org, modified 31 July 2026, https://aboutcoffee.org/origins/coffee-regions-of-the-world/

facts.text: The European Union and the United States are the largest coffee importers (USDA "Total Imports" table order: European Union, United States, Japan).
facts.source: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Coffee: World Markets and Trade, July 2026, https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/circulars/coffee.pdf

shots.title: 184 million bags
shots.show: The whole globe, dark navy oceans and slate land, turning slowly. Small coffee-bean pins pop up one after another around the equator while a big gold rolling counter at the top climbs to ≈184 million and lands with a bounce, the unit 'bags / year' beneath it.
shots.text: ≈184 million bags a year. From where?
shots.motion: Globe rotates; bean pins pop in with a small bounce in a ripple along the equator; counter rolls from 0 and bounces on 184,000,000.
shots.source: ICO Coffee Market Report, Aug 2026 (2025/26 estimate, 60-kg bags)

shots.title: The coffee belt
shots.show: The globe unrolls into the flat world map. Two dashed lines draw on, labelled Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn; the band between them fills with a soft gold glow. Then the growing countries light leaf green one by one from the Americas to Africa to Asia, while a small counter beside the band ticks up to 40+.
shots.text: Grown in 40+ countries between the tropics
shots.motion: Globe-to-flat morph; tropic lines draw left to right; band fades in; country fills ripple west to east; counter ticks to 40+.

shots.title: Brazil leads
shots.show: Camera flies from the world into South America. Brazil fills a brighter leaf green and grows a gold pin with rank badge '1'. Beside it a big counter rolls to 40% under the word 'nearly', and a split bar at the bottom (the world's coffee) splits: Brazil's nearly 40% in green, the rest in dim slate.
shots.motion: Zoom and pan into Brazil; the fill pulses brighter; pin drops; counter rolls; split bar wipes and separates into its two shares.
shots.source: USDA FAS, Coffee: World Markets and Trade, July 2026 ("nearly 40 percent")

shots.title: The top five
shots.show: Camera pulls back out to the coffee belt. Rank pins drop in turn with their badges: 2 Vietnam (labelled 'robusta'), 3 Colombia, 4 Ethiopia, 5 Indonesia, each country brightening to the same leaf green as Brazil, which keeps its '1' pin.
shots.motion: Camera glides east across the belt; each pin drops with a bounce as the camera passes; country names type on beside the pins.
shots.source: USDA FAS, Coffee: World Markets and Trade, July 2026

shots.title: Where coffee began
shots.show: Camera flies into East Africa. Ethiopia's highlands glow warm gold inside its green fill; its '4' pin stays, and a small coffee-plant icon sprouts on the highlands with the label 'coffee forests'. Faint ripples spread from it across the map.
shots.motion: Zoom into the Horn of Africa; gold glow breathes; plant icon grows leaf by leaf; ripple rings expand outward.

shots.title: Routes north
shots.show: Camera pulls out to the full flat map with the belt and the five green producers. Coffee-orange arcs draw on from Brazil, Colombia, Vietnam, Indonesia and Ethiopia to two destinations that light cool blue: the European Union and the United States. Small bean dots run along every arc like a flow.
shots.text: Most sails north to Europe and the US
shots.motion: Arcs draw on one after another; destination fills fade in blue; bean dots stream continuously along the arcs; camera drifts slowly north.
shots.source: USDA FAS, Coffee: World Markets and Trade, July 2026 (largest importers)

shots.title: End card
shots.show: The globe again, slowly turning, wrapped in the glowing orange routes from the previous shot, bean dots still flowing; the title 'Where does the world's coffee come from' settles above it.
shots.motion: Globe turns; arcs shimmer; bean dots keep running; title fades and settles.

recurring.name: World map with the coffee belt
recurring.design: Navy ocean, slate-grey land; the coffee belt is a soft gold band between two dashed tropic lines labelled at the left edge; growing countries in leaf green (meaning: where coffee grows), always the same green.

recurring.name: Rank pins
recurring.design: Gold teardrop pins with a white numeric badge 1–5 (Brazil 1, Vietnam 2, Colombia 3, Ethiopia 4, Indonesia 5), country name in white type to the right of the pin; once dropped they stay.

recurring.name: Trade routes
recurring.design: Coffee-orange arcs bowing north from each top-five producer to its destination, with small bean-shaped dots flowing along them; importing destinations (EU, US) fill cool blue (meaning: where coffee goes).
